["EO 8044 is not supported for submission: its ends are not shown for all of its operative parts. Section 1 suspends Executive Order No. 7916 \"until further order\" for five classes of positions, section 2 defines administrative and technical positions, and section 3 appoints a committee to study and report; the dossier's ten machine-segmented clauses (EO:8044#1, a, b, c, d, e, e-2, a-dup2, b-dup2, b-3) are not this structure and would need an inventory correction to three scopes before any claim.","Section 1: the only held instrument that ends it, EO 8743 section 7 (April 23, 1941), revokes EO 8044 only so far as it applies to positions covered into the classified civil service by that order, and EO 8743 section 1 does not cover temporary positions, positions excepted by statute, positions in Schedules A and B of the Civil Service Rules, or positions already classified. No held source shows that the suspension of EO 7916 for the five classes of positions in section 1 (including the Inland Waterways Corporation positions and the positions found impracticable to fill by competitive examination or highly confidential) ended as to the positions outside EO 8743 section 1, so a first-end date for the whole of section 1 is not established.","Section 3: the committee reported (EO 8743 section 3(a) cites its report as House Document No. 118, 77th Congress), but a report is a spent fact and not an end; EOs 8371, 8372 and 8373 (March 9, 1940) amend section 3 and EO 9230 is a later order that recites EO 8044; no held instrument revokes EO 8044 section 3 or dissolves the committee. Missing source: a held order or other instrument revoking or terminating section 3 and the suspension in section 1 as to the remaining positions."]

["EO 8051 is not supported for submission: its own terms give two possible ends and the held record cannot fix which came first. The order limits imports of red cedar shingles from Canada for the first six months of calendar year 1939 (a fixed period ending June 30, 1939) and, in its last sentence, provides that upon the termination in whole of the trade agreement with Canada of November 15, 1935, in accordance with Article XVIII of the trade agreement signed November 17, 1938, the order ceases to have force and effect. A contingent own-terms end earlier than the fixed period would control.","Missing source: the text of the trade agreement between the United States and Canada signed November 17, 1938 (Article XVIII and its entry-into-force provision), and the proclamation or Federal Register notice fixing the date on which the 1935 agreement terminated. No held order text or other held source states that date, so it is not established whether the contingent end occurred before, on or after June 30, 1939, or whether it had already occurred before the order was made on February 15, 1939."]
